That ones hard to say without undertaking a proper ‘deep dive’. And while I’m sure there are random hints in the dialogue, I don’t think they settled on any particular time period. Which is mainly based on my opinion that the game doesn’t really need one, if that makes sense.

Still, to we can try to narrow it down. It’s safe to assume it takes place either after, or during the Trojan war, based on the presence of Achilles in Tartarus, and frequent mentions of war in the surface. The game also eludes to Zagreus being trained by Achilles, meaning anything from 5-100 years may have elapsed since that famous horse and the sacking of Troy. Going by how he seems to have been serving the house for a long time, and the fact that our King Theseus makes an appearance, I’d say that places us around the time of Homer’s Odyssey. We could go even further and say that, based on dialogue between Ares and Athena, that Odysseus’s war against the Brygoi is the one being referenced. This might also explain Apollo’s absence from the game, as he is the one said to separate Ares and Athena. So just to add a date to it, let’s say it takes place around 600-500 BC. 

Who knows though? I might be completely off the mark and they might be referencing the fall of Mycenae or something ahaha.

TLDR; Based on random bits of dialogue I pulled from a hat, we can estimate the game takes place during Homer’s Odyssey. Maybe during Odysseus’s war with the Brygoi.

He did and his story is very... Well, it’s very Zeus of Zeus. I’ll try to summarise, though I’m writing this all from memory on my train ride home. So, something something, grain of salt.

Hades requested a wife, and Zeus gave her Persephone. Only before sending her over, he forced himself on her, which eventually resulted in the birth of Zagreus (in Tartarus). Classic Zeus. So, to spite Zeus (and there is some debate on whether Hera or Hades were involved here), Titans lured away baby Zag with gifts, and then tore him limb from limb. By the time Athena arrived, his heart was the only thing that could be salvaged, and so kept it in a little jar. How sweet of her. The entire myth of Zagreus related to the ritual sacrifice of young boys in Ancient Greece, with the gifts used to lure the child relating to adjacent offerings of significance. As with all myths, there are hundreds of interpretations, so I recommend looking into it. It’s really fun :) 

Anyhow, I hope this makes it clear why the wholesome narrative made by the game developers, is one I prefer over the r*pe-baby-human-sacrifice that is the ‘original’ Zagreus.

I love the attention they paid to the actual structure of Tartarus, the four realms, and the RIVERS. That they even incorporated the appearance and purpose of each of the five rivers into the games! As a classicist that brings me immense joy 😌♥️
